clue.text: Traveller with one large bird going after another around English river runs away

indicators.note: the two large birds stand either side of the English letter, so together they sit around it

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
the emu is a large flightless Australian bird
another large bird: L for large again, this time with a gull

indicators.note: something that runs away leaves, so the runs letter is taken out of the river

parts.note: the word river taken as written
R is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A wanderer watches a big bird chasing another past an English stream before fleeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another large bird, so 'large' serves both birds; 'away' drops the runs letter from the river, leaving IVER. The River Ver is a real English river, a decoy here.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift's hero is the most famous voyager in English satire, visiting Lilliput and other strange lands.

clue.text: Get rid of Miss Harker among the very best

indicators.note: among says one piece is placed within the letters of the other

parts.note: the elite are the very best of a group
Mina Harker is the heroine of Bram Stoker's Dracula

explanation.surface: Someone wants to remove Dracula's heroine from a top-flight group.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate is to remove or do away with something.

clue.text: Re the Ashes prize, Australia, Lord's leaders, reportedly deserve coming first

indicators.note: coming first places the sound-alike at the front of the build
reportedly signals that the word for deserve is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to earn something is to deserve it
A is the international vehicle code for Australia

indicators.note: the leaders of a word are its opening letters, here just the initial of Lord's

explanation.surface: A note on cricket's famous trophy, with Australia at Lord's earning first place.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes, contested by England and Australia, are kept in a small urn, often shown at Lord's, the London cricket ground; the answer is an adjective, so 'Re the Ashes prize' means relating to that urn.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something relating to a vase-like vessel, and the Ashes trophy is such a vessel.

clue.text: Chazelle's land, a place to see animals drink up — that's excellent

parts.note: Damien Chazelle directed the film La La Land

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the run of pieces is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a zoo is where animals are kept for viewing
to lap is to drink as a cat does

explanation.surface: A film director's world, a zoo, and animals drinking, all declared splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole three-piece run at once, not just the drink, which is why the zoo ends up reading backwards as well.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang word names an outstanding or remarkable person or thing.

clue.text: If Wilde was right the fox would have been after the hunt

definitions.text: If Wilde was right the fox would have been after the hunt

parts.words: If Wilde was right the fox would have been after the hunt
parts.note: Oscar Wilde called fox hunting the unspeakable in full pursuit of the uneatable, so a fox nobody can eat stays on the plate untouched

explanation.definitionFit: Something not consumed remains intact, as an inedible quarry would be.

clue.text: Look back to inspect? His wife did

definitions.text: Look back to inspect? His wife did

parts.words: Look back to inspect? His wife did
parts.note: in Genesis a man fleeing Sodom had a wife who looked back and became a pillar of salt

explanation.definitionFit: The biblical nephew of Abraham fled Sodom, and his wife turned to look and was punished.

clue.text: Dairy Sven's converted to areas of specialized farming

indicators.note: converted says the letters are changed into a new form

parts.note: the possessive s gives no letter

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian farmer's dairy has been turned over to another use.
explanation.definitionFit: Grape-growing plots are farmland given over to a single specialist crop.

clue.text: Drummer taking band to Ohio

parts.note: a ring is a circular band

explanation.surface: A percussionist takes his group on tour to Ohio.
explanation.definitionFit: Starr played drums for the Beatles.

clue.text: Politician if set back by Chiltern finally gains heart of Effingham

indicators.note: set back says the little word is turned round, written backwards
finally picks the closing letter of Chiltern
the heart of a word is its central letter, here of Effingham

explanation.surface: Political news from the Home Counties: a candidate in the Chilterns and Effingham.
explanation.walkthrough: Phineas, the title character of Trollope's novel, is an Irish MP; the Chiltern Hundreds is the post an MP takes to resign.
explanation.definitionFit: Trollope's Palliser novels follow this young Irish member of parliament.

clue.text: Story you heard accompanied by score about soldier Kijé, for example

parts.note: a story can be a lie or fib

indicators.note: heard says the word is taken as it sounds, giving a single letter

parts.note: the word you is said like the letter U

indicators.note: about says the word for score is turned round

parts.note: to net is to score a goal
a soldier ant is a caste of ant that defends the colony

explanation.surface: A story set to music about a soldier, the Kijé of Prokofiev's score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses NET to TEN. Lieutenant Kijé is Prokofiev's film score about a fictional officer, so 'score' and 'soldier' both look like part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Kijé is a fictional officer whose rank appears in the title of Prokofiev's suite.

clue.text: Dietrich's persona expressed going around lost island

indicators.note: going around says one piece wraps the other

parts.note: Marlene Dietrich made famous the song Lili Marleen
L is an abbreviation for lost, as in league tables
to put something is to express it, as in well put

explanation.surface: A film star's character is voiced on a trip around a vanished island.
explanation.definitionFit: The land of tiny people is the first place visited in Swift's satire.

clue.text: Unpopular captain heard to name one who described The Ship of Adventure

definitions.text: one who described The Ship of Adventure

indicators.note: heard says the captain's name is taken as it sounds

parts.note: Captain Bligh of the Bounty was so unpopular his crew mutinied
taken as written

explanation.surface: A notorious ship's captain is mentioned beside a children's author.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ship of Adventure is one of the Adventure series of children's books by Enid, the prolific English author.

clue.text: Go and bring band round, where a large crowd will be found

definitions.text: where a large crowd will be found

indicators.note: round says the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to fetch a group of musicians for a big audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' acts on three words together; 'and' is only a link. 'large crowd' tempts as a word for many people, but Swift's giants make every crowd large.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift's land of giants is a place where every crowd is huge in size.

clue.text: Papal treasurer about to get wizard to leave

parts.note: CA, for circa, means about
Merlin is King Arthur's wizard
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: The Vatican's money man is told a wizard must depart.
explanation.definitionFit: The cardinal who administers the Holy See's property and revenues is its chamberlain and treasurer.

clue.text: "It isn't t —— to cut anyone you've been introduced to" (Lewis Carroll)

definitions.text: "It isn't t —— to cut anyone you've been introduced to" (Lewis Carroll)

parts.words: "It isn't t —— to cut anyone you've been introduced to" (Lewis Carroll)
parts.note: a fill-in quotation from Through the Looking-Glass, where the Red Queen lectures Alice on manners at the banquet

explanation.definitionFit: Good manners or social convention is the missing word the Red Queen invokes.

clue.text: Miss Keeler, what a gem!

definitions.meaning: Keeler was an American actress and dancer of 1930s musicals

explanation.definitionFit: The name of the dancer Keeler is also that of a red precious stone.

clue.text: Lord of the Flies, one appreciated even by Philistines

definitions.meaning: the Hebrew name of the demon is often translated this way
in the Bible Baal-zebub was the god of the Philistine city of Ekron

explanation.definitionFit: The demon's name means lord of flies, and he was worshipped as a god in Philistine Ekron.

clue.text: To whom Gilbert's lord's half-heartedly introduced initially

definitions.text: To whom Gilbert's lord's half-heartedly introduced initially

indicators.note: half-heartedly says half the central pair of letters goes

parts.note: Gilbert's Iolanthe is full of peers of the realm, and the 's stands for is

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of introduced

explanation.surface: In a Gilbert opera a nobleman is shyly presented to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Iolanthe's subtitle is The Peer and the Peri, the fairy a lord is introduced to.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy or sprite of Persian legend, the kind the House of Lords meets in Iolanthe.

clue.text: Drove around America with Hughes, say, covered in powder

indicators.note: around says the letters are moved about into a new order

parts.note: US is short for the United States
Ted Hughes was Poet Laureate; say marks him as one example of the name

explanation.surface: A road trip across the States with the poet Hughes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given too much of a fine sprinkling is overly coated in it.

clue.text: Result of an infection when Austen girl hugs Peake's evangelist

indicators.note: hugs says one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: Emma is the heroine of Jane Austen's novel
Mervyn Peake's novel Mr Pye has a title character set on converting Sark

explanation.surface: An Austen heroine embraces a Peake preacher at the moment of infection.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term names a collection of pus in a body cavity, a consequence of infection.

clue.text: Floating island you'll find heading west in boat up a lake

indicators.note: heading west says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Directions to a flying island on a boat trip westward across a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'heading west' reads right to left; 'in' signals the letters sit inside 'boat up a lake'.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift's flying island in Gulliver's Travels floats above the land it rules.

clue.text: Holmes's game was to get an answer at the end

parts.note: A is the usual abbreviation for answer
the foot is the bottom end of something, such as a bed

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes announces his game is to find a solution at last.
explanation.walkthrough: Holmes's line is 'The game is afoot', meaning under way; 'Holmes's game was' asks for that word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means under way or in progress, completing Holmes's famous phrase.

clue.text: "A brisk, — chef with a tall puffed cap on, half again as big as him ." (Bernard Malamud, The Natural)

definitions.text: "A brisk, — chef with a tall puffed cap on, half again as big as him ." (Bernard Malamud, The Natural)

parts.words: "A brisk, — chef with a tall puffed cap on, half again as big as him ." (Bernard Malamud, The Natural)
parts.note: a fill-in quotation from Malamud's baseball novel; the cap being half as big again as the chef shows the gap is a word for small

explanation.definitionFit: The missing word means small or diminutive, describing a short chef.

clue.text: Writer given direction by newspaper about start of item

parts.note: SW, south-west, is a compass direction

indicators.note: start of picks the opening letter of item

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times

explanation.surface: An author takes direction from a newspaper about the start of a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a container or reversal, but FT around I would give FIT; here the paper simply sits next to I.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift, Dublin dean and satirist, wrote Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: Back door affording entrance to 196Os fashionista, like Derrida or Lacan

indicators.note: a door affording entrance lets something in, so the back door holds the other piece

parts.note: a postern is a back or side gate
mods were the sharp-suited 1960s youth subculture

explanation.surface: A back door lets in a sixties dandy who talks like a French theorist.
explanation.definitionFit: Derrida and Lacan are French thinkers grouped with late twentieth-century theory that rejects modernist certainties.

clue.text: Pole with podagra, oddly neglected

indicators.note: neglecting the odd letters leaves the second, fourth and sixth of podagra

parts.note: the run across podagra and oddly that reads backwards as the answer is a coincidence; the alternate letters are the setter's device

explanation.surface: A Polish man suffering from gout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality; it is a long stick. Podagra is gout.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing blade is a long wooden shaft, a kind of pole.

clue.text: Alumnus, soldier, reverting to African language

indicators.note: reverting says the whole run of pieces is turned backwards

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A former pupil turned soldier returns to his native tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: This tongue is spoken by millions in south-eastern Nigeria.

clue.text: Target he shot with guns near shady bootlegger

indicators.note: shot says the letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: gats is slang for guns
by means near, as in stand by me

explanation.surface: A gangster with guns takes aim at a bootlegger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges TARGET HE. The answer is Fitzgerald's title, standing for its bootlegger hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitzgerald's mysterious hero made his fortune from illicit liquor.
